key_insight: SciDiagramEdit shows that scientific figures can be edited automatically from paper revisions by learning the patterns of how authors change diagrams over time. The key idea is to treat figure editing as a structured, instruction-driven task rather than generic image manipulation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the time-consuming task of revising scientific figures during manuscript updates, such as relabeling components, rearranging panels, and restyling visuals. It targets the difficulty of editing dense, heterogeneous diagrams under natural-language instructions while preserving scientific meaning and layout consistency.
method: Learns from paired paper revisions to model how scientific diagrams change across versions.
Uses natural-language instructions to guide localized edits on complex figures containing schematics, plots, photos, captions, and arrows.
Focuses on preserving the visual grammar of scientific graphics while performing targeted modifications.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this points toward tools that can assist with manuscript preparation and figure revision, reducing manual editing overhead. It is especially relevant for document AI, multimodal editing, and human-in-the-loop scientific workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing revision text input to edited figure output
Annotated diagram highlighting relabeled panels, moved components, and restyled elements
Icon set representing plots, schematics, photos, arrows, and captions
paper_title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
paper_authors: Yasheng Sun, Zezi Zeng, Yifan Yang, Chong Luo, Wenyi Wang
